articles.summary: Water Tower Research’s new research report takes a close look at how eXoZymes is moving from a promising scientific platform toward a potentially scalable commercial business. The report identifies NCT as the company’s most important near-term opportunity and highlights the dramatic progress made in taking it from laboratory development toward commercial production. It also explores the much larger opportunity behind the platform - including potential pharmaceutical applications, cannabinoids, santalene and a pipeline of new molecules - while outlining the milestones that could determine how quickly eXoZymes can turn its technology into partnerships, products and revenue. 7 things to know from the report:
articles.title: WTR: Converting Cell-Free Science into a Scalable and Repeatable Commercial Opportunity

articles.summary: October 22 investor event will explore eXoZymes’ commercialization, manufacturing economics, path to market launch, growth strategy, and milestones ahead. Los Angeles, CA -- October 21, 2026 -- Today, eXoZymes Inc. (NASDAQ: EXOZ) (“eXoZymes”) - a pioneer of AI-enhanced enzymes that transform abundant feedstock into valuable nutraceuticals and novel medicines - announced that Chief Executive Officer, Michael Heltzen, will participate in a fireside chat hosted by Water Tower Research (“WTR”) tomorrow, Thursday, October 22, 2026, at 11AM Eastern / 8AM Pacific Time.
articles.title: CEO to discuss commercialization, key milestones, and potential catalysts in fireside chat with WTR

articles.summary: Recap AI is revolutionizing drug discovery. But there’s a billion-dollar problem nobody talks about: Making what AI discovers. As artificial intelligence unlocks an entirely new world of molecules and potential medicines, traditional manufacturing may struggle to keep pace. In this Mashable feature , discover how eXoZymes is working to bridge the gap between AI-powered discovery and real-world production - potentially changing how tomorrow’s medicines are made.
articles.title: Mashable: AI is accelerating Drug Discovery. Can manufacturing keep up?
